records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: spoke ... saying: the opening of a new speech
decisions.reason: The usual opening of a speech of God to Moses, as in 1:1. This speech, on the holy food of the priests, runs to verse 16.

records.heading: Who may eat the holy food

records.source: דַּבֵּ֨ר אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֜ן וְאֶל־בָּנָ֗יו וְיִנָּֽזְרוּ֙ מִקָּדְשֵׁ֣י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְלֹ֥א יְחַלְּל֖וּ אֶת־שֵׁ֣ם קָדְשִׁ֑י אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵ֧ם מַקְדִּשִׁ֛ים לִ֖י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Speak to Aaron and to his sons, and they will separate themselves from [the] holy things of [the] sons of Israel, and not they will profane [the] name of my holiness, which they [are] consecrating to me; I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: "Tell Aaron and his sons to be careful with the holy gifts that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} set apart for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and so not profane {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.2: "Speak to Aaron and to his sons, that they keep themselves apart from the holy things of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and [that] they not profane {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name, [the things] which they consecrate to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.2: "Tell Aaron and his sons to be careful with the holy gifts that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} set apart for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Then they will not dishonor {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the holy things: the gifts Israel sets apart for God, including the food the priests eat
decisions.reason: The word covers everything the people consecrate to God: the priests' portions of the sacrifices (6:9-11; 7:31-34; 10:12-15), the firstfruits, the tithes and things given by vow (Numbers 18:8-19). They belong to God, and the priests and their households eat them as his gift. This chapter is mostly about that holy food. The clause "which they consecrate to me" comes after "my holy name" in Hebrew, but it describes the holy things: it is the Israelites who set them apart for God, as verse 3 says.

decisions.choice: keep themselves apart from: hold back from the holy things whenever they may not touch them
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for a Nazirite, one set apart (Numbers 6:2). It means to separate oneself from something, to hold back from it, and so to treat it with reverence. Verses 3-9 show what is meant: a priest who is unclean must not come near the holy things or eat them until he is clean.

decisions.choice: profane my holy name: treat what belongs to God as common, and so dishonor God himself
decisions.reason: To profane is to make common, to take what is holy into ordinary use (19:12; 21:6). God's name stands for God himself as he has made himself known (Exodus 3:15; 20:7). When a priest handles the holy gifts carelessly, the dishonor falls on the God to whom they belong. "My holy name" is literally "the name of my holiness" (20:3; Ezekiel 36:20-23). The same warning closes the chapter (verse 32).

decisions.choice: be careful with the holy gifts
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the separation means in practice, following m2: the priests must take care with the holy gifts and not touch them when unclean. Literal keeps "keep themselves apart from the holy things".

decisions.choice: dishonor
decisions.reason: Readable says "dishonor" for "profane", the common word for what profaning God's name does. Literal and Balanced keep "profane".

decisions.choice: [the things] which they consecrate to me
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the clause in its Hebrew place and supplies "the things" so that it is not read as describing the name. Balanced and Readable move it next to "the holy gifts", which it describes.

records.source: אֱמֹ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם לְדֹרֹ֨תֵיכֶ֜ם כָּל־אִ֣ישׁ׀אֲשֶׁר־יִקְרַ֣ב מִכָּל־זַרְעֲכֶ֗ם אֶל־הַקֳּדָשִׁים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַקְדִּ֤ישׁוּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְטֻמְאָת֖וֹ עָלָ֑יו וְנִכְרְתָ֞ה הַנֶּ֧פֶשׁ הַהִ֛וא מִלְּפָנַ֖י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Say to them, for your generations, every man who draws near from all your offspring to the holy things which consecrate [the] sons of Israel to Yahweh, and his uncleanness [is] on him, and will be cut off the person that from before me; I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: Say to them: 'For all your generations, if any man among your descendants comes near the holy gifts that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} consecrate to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} while he is unclean, that person must be cut off from before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'

L.3: Say to them, 'For your generations, any man of all your offspring who comes near to the holy things that the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel consecrate to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} while his uncleanness [is] on him, that person shall be cut off from before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'

R.3: Tell them, 'For all time to come, none of your descendants may come near the holy gifts while he is unclean. These are the gifts the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} set apart as holy for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Anyone who does so must be removed from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'

decisions.choice: comes near ... while his uncleanness is on him: handles or eats the holy things while unclean
decisions.reason: To come near the holy things is to touch them or eat them (verses 4-7). The man meant is any descendant of Aaron, a priest by birth. The danger is not the holy food itself but a priest bringing his uncleanness into contact with what is holy (7:20-21; 15:31).

decisions.choice: cut off from before me: removed from God's presence
decisions.reason: This is the penalty of being cut off (7:20), here put as "from before me": the priest who serves in God's presence loses his place before him. It is God who acts, as in 20:3-6.

decisions.choice: three short sentences
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long Hebrew sentence into the rule, the description of the holy gifts and the penalty.

records.source: אִ֣ישׁ אִ֞ישׁ מִזֶּ֣רַע אַהֲרֹ֗ן וְה֤וּא צָר֨וּעַ֙ א֣וֹ זָ֔ב בַּקֳּדָשִׁים֙ לֹ֣א יֹאכַ֔ל עַ֖ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִטְהָ֑ר וְהַנֹּגֵ֨עַ֙ בְּכָל־טְמֵא־נֶ֔פֶשׁ א֣וֹ אִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־תֵּצֵ֥א מִמֶּ֖נּוּ שִׁכְבַת־זָֽרַע׃
records.gloss: [A] man, [a] man of [the] offspring of Aaron, and he [has a] scale disease or [a] discharge, in the holy things not he will eat until that he is clean; and the [one] who touches any unclean [by a] person, or [a] man who goes out from him [an] emission of seed,
pieces: No man descended from Aaron who has a serious skin disease or a discharge may eat any of the holy food until he is clean. Nor may one who touches anything made unclean by a dead body, or a man who has an emission of semen,

L.4: Any man of the offspring of Aaron who has scale disease or a discharge shall not eat of the holy things until he is clean. And whoever touches anything unclean through a dead person, or a man from whom an emission of semen goes out,

R.4: A man from Aaron's family who has a serious skin disease or a discharge from his body must not eat the holy food until he is clean. The same is true if he touches something made unclean by a dead body, or if semen comes out of his body.

decisions.choice: scale disease or a discharge: the long-lasting kinds of uncleanness
decisions.reason: Scale disease (13:2) and a discharge from the body (15:2) last until they heal, and the man is then cleansed with offerings (14:1-32; 15:13-15). Until then the priest may not eat the holy food. The other cases in verses 4-6 last only until evening.

decisions.choice: unclean through a dead person: made unclean by contact with a corpse
decisions.reason: The word for person here means a dead person, as in 21:1, 11 and Numbers 19:11-13. Whatever has touched a corpse passes the uncleanness on.

decisions.choice: or a man from whom an emission of semen goes out: the priest himself, as in 15:16
alternatives: or who touches a man who has an emission of semen
decisions.reason: The clause most likely describes the priest himself, in a series of cases each opened by "or a man" (verse 5). It may instead continue "whoever touches": one who touches a man who has had an emission. Either way the uncleanness lasts until evening (15:16-17).

decisions.choice: any man / no man
decisions.reason: The doubled word means "any man" (17:3). These laws are for the priests, so no gender setting is used. Balanced puts the ruling first as "No man ... may eat" and carries it into the cases that follow.

decisions.choice: The same is true if ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence runs on to the end of verse 6. Readable gives each case in a sentence of its own.

records.source: אוֹ־אִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִגַּ֔ע בְּכָל־שֶׁ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִטְמָא־ל֑וֹ א֤וֹ בְאָדָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִטְמָא־ל֔וֹ לְכֹ֖ל טֻמְאָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: or [a] man who touches any swarming thing which makes him unclean, or [a] human who makes him unclean, with all his uncleanness,
pieces: or one who touches any swarming creature that makes him unclean, or a human being through whom he becomes unclean in any of the ways a person can be unclean,

L.5: or a man who touches any swarming thing by which he becomes unclean, or a human being by whom he becomes unclean, whatever his uncleanness,

R.5: It is also true if he touches any small creature that makes him unclean, or a person who makes him unclean in any way.

decisions.choice: swarming thing: small creatures that teem on the ground
decisions.reason: The word covers small creatures such as rats, mice and lizards. Touching their bodies makes a person unclean until evening (11:29-31).

decisions.choice: a human being ... whatever his uncleanness: anyone whose uncleanness passes to the priest
decisions.reason: Some kinds of uncleanness in people pass to those who touch them, such as a discharge (15:7) or a woman's flow (15:19). "Whatever his uncleanness" covers every such kind. The word for human being is the general word, not the word for a man.

records.source: נֶ֚פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּגַּע־בּ֔וֹ וְטָמְאָ֖ה עַד־הָעָ֑רֶב וְלֹ֤א יֹאכַל֙ מִן־הַקֳּדָשִׁ֔ים כִּ֛י אִם־רָחַ֥ץ בְּשָׂר֖וֹ בַּמָּֽיִם׃
records.gloss: [a] person who touches it will be unclean until the evening, and not he will eat from the holy things except if he has washed his flesh in water.
pieces: the one who has touched it stays unclean until evening and may not eat any of the holy food until he has washed his body in water.

L.6: the person who touches it shall be unclean until the evening, and shall not eat of the holy things unless he has bathed his body in water.

R.6: Any priest who touches such things will be unclean until evening. He must not eat any of the holy food until he has washed his body with water.

decisions.choice: unclean until evening, and washed: two steps to being clean again
decisions.reason: The priest bathes, and his uncleanness ends at sunset (verse 7). Only then may he eat. The same pattern is found in 11:24-25 and 15:5-11. For the holy food, the bath is required, not optional.

decisions.choice: Any priest
decisions.reason: Readable names the person: the cases in verses 4-6 are about Aaron's descendants.

records.source: וּבָ֥א הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ וְטָהֵ֑ר וְאַחַר֙ יֹאכַ֣ל מִן־הַקֳּדָשִׁ֔ים כִּ֥י לַחְמ֖וֹ הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And goes the sun, and he will be clean, and after he will eat from the holy things, for his food it [is].
pieces: Once the sun has set he is clean, and then he may eat of the holy food, since that is what he lives on.

L.7: And the sun shall go down, and he will be clean; and afterward he may eat of the holy things, for it [is] his food.

R.7: After the sun goes down, he will be clean. Then he may eat the holy food. It is the food the priests live on.

decisions.choice: it is his food: the priests live on the holy gifts
decisions.reason: The priests had no land of their own. Their food was their share of the offerings (Numbers 18:8-20; Deuteronomy 18:1-2). So the rule does not take the food away: it only makes him wait until he is clean.

decisions.choice: what he lives on
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "his food" means here, following m1. Literal keeps "his food".

records.source: נְבֵלָ֧ה וּטְרֵפָ֛ה לֹ֥א יֹאכַ֖ל לְטָמְאָה־בָ֑הּ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: A carcass or [a] torn [animal] not he will eat, to become unclean by it; I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: He must not eat an animal that has died or one torn by wild beasts, and so become unclean by it. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.8: A carcass or a torn [animal] he shall not eat, becoming unclean by it. I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.8: A priest must not eat an animal that died by itself or was killed by wild animals. It would make him unclean. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a carcass or a torn animal: meat from an animal that was not slaughtered
decisions.reason: The blood of such an animal was not drained out (17:13-15). An ordinary Israelite who ate it became unclean until evening and had to wash (11:40; 17:15). For a priest it is forbidden outright, as Ezekiel 44:31 repeats.

decisions.choice: A priest
decisions.reason: Readable names who is meant, as in verse 6.

records.source: וְשָׁמְר֣וּ אֶת־מִשְׁמַרְתִּ֗י וְלֹֽא־יִשְׂא֤וּ עָלָיו֙ חֵ֔טְא וּמֵ֥תוּ ב֖וֹ כִּ֣י יְחַלְּלֻ֑הוּ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה מְקַדְּשָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And they will keep my charge, and not they will bear on it sin and die by it, for they profane it; I [am] Yahweh [who] makes them holy.
pieces: The priests must guard what I have entrusted to them, or they will bear sin because of the holy food and die for having profaned it. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who makes them holy.

L.9: And they shall keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} charge, and they shall not bear sin for it and die by it, because they profane it. I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who makes them holy.

R.9: The priests must obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} orders. If they do not, they will be guilty because of the holy food. They will die for treating it as if it were not holy. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who makes them holy.

decisions.choice: my charge: the duty I have given them to guard
decisions.reason: The word means something kept or guarded, and so an obligation. It is used of the priests' and Levites' duties at the sanctuary (8:35; Numbers 3:7-8; 18:3-5). Here it is the duty of keeping the holy food from being made common.

decisions.choice: for it ... by it ... profane it: the holy food
decisions.reason: "It" has no stated noun. It most likely means the holy food of verses 2-7, which the priest profanes by eating it while unclean. To bear sin is to carry its guilt and its penalty (19:17; 24:15).

decisions.choice: I am the LORD who makes them holy: God himself sets the priests apart
decisions.reason: The priests were made holy at their ordination (8:12, 30), but it is God who makes them holy (21:8, 15, 23). Because they belong to him, they must treat what is holy as his. See verse 32.

decisions.choice: The priests; the holy food
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who "they" are and what "it" is, following m2.

records.source: וְכָל־זָ֖ר לֹא־יֹ֣אכַל קֹ֑דֶשׁ תּוֹשַׁ֥ב כֹּהֵ֛ן וְשָׂכִ֖יר לֹא־יֹ֥אכַל קֹֽדֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: And any stranger not he will eat [a] holy thing; [a] settler of [a] priest and [a] hired worker not he will eat [a] holy thing.
pieces: No layperson may eat holy food. Neither a resident staying with a priest nor a worker he hires may eat it.

L.10: And no stranger shall eat a holy thing; a settler of a priest or a hired worker shall not eat a holy thing.

R.10: Only a priest's family may eat holy food. A person who lives with a priest or works for him for pay must not eat it.

decisions.choice: stranger: anyone outside a priest's household, a layperson
decisions.reason: The word means one who is outside, an outsider to a particular group. Here it is anyone who does not belong to the household of a priest, even an Israelite (Numbers 3:10; 16:40; 18:4, 7). It is not the word for a sojourner (16:29) or for a foreigner (verse 25). Verses 10-13 then say who belongs to the household and who does not.

decisions.choice: a settler of a priest or a hired worker: people who live or work with a priest but are not his
decisions.reason: A settler is a resident without land of his own who lodges with others (25:6, 40), and a hired worker is paid by the day or the year (19:13). They may live in the priest's house, but they keep their freedom and are not part of his household. So they may not share its holy food.

decisions.choice: No layperson (Balanced); Only a priest's family (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Stranger" here does not mean a foreigner, so Balanced says "layperson" and Readable says who may eat. Literal keeps "stranger".

records.source: וְכֹהֵ֗ן כִּֽי־יִקְנֶ֥ה נֶ֨פֶשׁ֙ קִנְיַ֣ן כַּסְפּ֔וֹ ה֖וּא יֹ֣אכַל בּ֑וֹ וִילִ֣יד בֵּית֔וֹ הֵ֖ם יֹאכְל֥וּ בְלַחְמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And [a] priest, when he buys [a] person, [the] purchase of his money, he will eat of it; and [the] born of his house, they will eat of his food.
pieces: But a person whom a priest has bought with his money may eat of it, and so may the slaves born in his house. They may share his food.

L.11: But if a priest buys a person, the purchase of his money, he may eat of it; and those born in his house, they may eat of his food.

R.11: But if a priest buys a slave, the slave may eat the holy food. So may slaves born in the priest's house. They may eat the priest's food.

decisions.choice: a person, bought with his money: a slave, who belongs to the priest's household
decisions.reason: A slave bought with money was part of the household, unlike the settler or the hired worker of verse 10. Such a slave was circumcised and ate the Passover with the family (Genesis 17:12-13; Exodus 12:44-45). So the slave may also eat the holy food. On slaves in Israel see 25:44-46.

decisions.choice: those born in his house: slaves born into the household
decisions.reason: The phrase means slaves born to slaves already in the house (Genesis 17:12; Jeremiah 2:14). They too belong to the household.

decisions.choice: slave(s)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "a person" and "those born in his house". Balanced says "slaves born in his house", and Readable says "slave" for both, following m1 and m2. "Slave" stays, as the style guide keeps it for people bought with money.

records.source: וּבַת־כֹּהֵ֔ן כִּ֥י תִהְיֶ֖ה לְאִ֣ישׁ זָ֑ר הִ֕וא בִּתְרוּמַ֥ת הַקֳּדָשִׁ֖ים לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And [a] daughter of [a] priest, when she becomes [the wife] of [a] man [who is a] stranger, she of [the] contribution of the holy things not she will eat.
pieces: A priest's daughter who is married to a layman may not eat from the holy portions set aside as contributions.

L.12: And a daughter of a priest, if she belongs to a man [who is] a stranger, she shall not eat of the contribution of the holy things.

R.12: If a priest's daughter marries a man who is not from a priest's family, she must not eat the holy food set apart for the priests.

decisions.choice: belongs to a man who is a stranger: marries a man outside the priestly families
decisions.reason: "To be to a man" means to become his wife (Ruth 1:12-13). A married daughter becomes part of her husband's household. If he is not a priest, she no longer shares the holy food of her father's house.

decisions.choice: the contribution of the holy things: the holy portions set aside for the priests
decisions.reason: A contribution is what is lifted off and set aside from a larger whole for God and his priests, such as the thigh of the peace offering (7:32-34; 10:14-15) and the gifts listed in Numbers 18:11, 19. These were holy but not most holy, and the priest's daughters could eat them while they lived in his house (10:14).

decisions.choice: married to a layman / marries a man who is not from a priest's family
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "belongs to a man who is a stranger" means, following m1 and verse 10.

records.source: וּבַת־כֹּהֵן֩ כִּ֨י תִהְיֶ֜ה אַלְמָנָ֣ה וּגְרוּשָׁ֗ה וְזֶרַע֮ אֵ֣ין לָהּ֒ וְשָׁבָ֞ה אֶל־בֵּ֤ית אָבִ֨יהָ֙ כִּנְעוּרֶ֔יהָ מִלֶּ֥חֶם אָבִ֖יהָ תֹּאכֵ֑ל וְכָל־זָ֖ר לֹא־יֹ֥אכַל בּֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: And [a] daughter of [a] priest, when she becomes [a] widow or divorced, and offspring there is not to her, and she returns to [the] house of her father as [in] her youth, from [the] food of her father she will eat; and any stranger not he will eat of it.
pieces: But a priest's daughter who has lost her husband through death or divorce, who has no children, and who has returned to her father's house as when she was a girl, may again share her father's food. Still, no layperson may eat it.

L.13: But a daughter of a priest, if she becomes a widow or divorced and has no offspring, and returns to the house of her father as in her youth, she may eat of the food of her father; but no stranger shall eat of it.

R.13: But a priest's daughter may become a widow or be divorced. If she has no children and comes back to live in her father's house, as she did when she was young, she may eat her father's food. But no one outside a priest's family may eat it.

decisions.choice: a widow or divorced, with no children, back in her father's house: she belongs to his household again
decisions.reason: With no husband and no children to support her, she returns to her father's house and is again counted in his household, as she was before her marriage. A widow or divorced woman who had children would belong with them. Tamar returned to her father's house in this way (Genesis 38:11).

decisions.choice: the food of her father: the holy food of verse 12
decisions.reason: Her father's food is the holy portions he receives as a priest (verse 7). She may share them again, but they remain closed to anyone outside the household (verse 10).

decisions.choice: who has lost her husband through death or divorce
decisions.reason: Balanced joins "widow or divorced" in one phrase. Literal and Readable keep the two words.

decisions.choice: for your acceptance: so that God accepts you, the ones who offer

decisions.reason: The word means favor, goodwill or acceptance. With "your" it is the worshiper who is accepted, not only the animal (1:3-4): God receives the person through the offering. The phrase is the key to verses 19-29. An offering with a defect is "not for your acceptance" (verse 20), and the thanksgiving offering must be made "for your acceptance" (verse 29). Offering God something damaged is offering him what he will not accept (Malachi 1:8, 13).

decisions.choice: unblemished, a male: the rule for a burnt offering
decisions.reason: A burnt offering from the herd or the flock must be a male without defect (1:3, 10). On "unblemished" see 1:3; verses 22-24 list what counts as a defect.

decisions.choice: for your acceptance, ... / then, to be accepted for you, ...
decisions.reason: Verse 19 completes the sentence begun in verse 18. Literal keeps the Hebrew order and supplies "it shall be"; Balanced adds "then" to show where the ruling begins. Readable starts a new sentence.

decisions.reason: Readable makes the LORD the subject. He is the one who accepts or refuses (verse 19).

pieces: If {{gender:anyone|any man}} brings {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a peace offering from the herd or the flock, whether to pay a vow or as a freewill offering, the animal must be without defect if it is to be accepted. There must be nothing at all wrong with it.

L.21: And if {{gender:anyone|a man}} brings near a sacrifice of peace offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering, from the herd or from the flock, it shall be unblemished to be accepted; there shall be no blemish in it.

The animal must have nothing wrong with it, or {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will not accept it. It must not have any flaw at all.

decisions.choice: to fulfill a vow: to pay what was promised
decisions.reason: The verb is used in 27:2 and Numbers 6:2; 15:3, 8 with "vow". It may mean to carry out a vow, or to make a special vow, one set apart from the ordinary. Here, with an offering already being brought, carrying out the vow fits best.

decisions.choice: unblemished for acceptance: the same rule for peace offerings as for burnt offerings
decisions.reason: The peace offering (3:1), of either sex (3:1, 6), must be just as sound as the burnt offering. Only for the freewill offering is a small exception allowed (verse 23). On "for acceptance" see verse 19.

decisions.choice: anyone / any man
decisions.reason: As in verse 18, the default is inclusive.

R.22: Do not offer {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} an animal that is blind, has a broken bone, or has been badly cut. Do not offer one with an oozing wound, a bad skin rash, or sores. Never put such an animal on the altar as a food offering burned for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: blind, broken, maimed: defects of sight and limb
decisions.reason: The first word is clear. The second means broken, most likely a broken bone or limb. The third comes from a verb meaning to cut or to sharpen, and occurs only here. It probably means an animal with a cut or a mutilated part, but the exact injury is not known.

decisions.choice: running sore, festering rash, scabs: skin conditions, the exact kinds unknown
decisions.reason: The first word occurs only here. It comes from a verb meaning to flow, and so may be a running sore, though wart has also been suggested. The second and third are the festering rash and scabs of 21:20 (see the note there; compare Deuteronomy 28:27). They are the same kinds of defect that bar a priest from serving at the altar (21:18-20).

decisions.choice: a broken limb, maimed (Balanced); a broken bone, badly cut, an oozing wound, a bad skin rash (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the defects in common words, following m1 and m2, and use the same words as 21:20 for the festering rash and scabs. Literal keeps the bare words, as the Hebrew lists them.

decisions.choice: a limb too long or stunted: a part of the body too long or too short

decisions.reason: The first word is used in 21:18 of a defect in a priest (see the note there). It seems to mean that a limb has grown too long or out of proportion. The second, found only here, seems to mean shrunken or stunted. The part of the body is not named.

decisions.choice: one leg too long or too short
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likely sense, following m1. As in 21:18, it speaks of a leg, since the Hebrew does not say which part.

decisions.reason: Literal keeps both words, "an offering, an offering by fire". Balanced keeps both with the settled "a food offering"; Readable gives one phrase.

records.gloss: And [an] ox or [a] sheep, it and its young not you will slaughter in day one.
pieces: Whether from the herd or the flock, a mother animal and its young must not both be slaughtered in a single day.

L.28: And an ox or a sheep, it and its young you shall not slaughter in one day.

R.28: Never kill a mother cow or sheep and its baby on the same day.

decisions.choice: it and its young: the mother and her offspring
alternatives: a parent animal and its young
decisions.reason: After verse 27, "it" is most naturally the mother of the young animal. The Hebrew pronoun is masculine, agreeing with "ox", the word for one of the herd of either sex. The law forbids killing a mother and her young on the same day, whether for sacrifice or for food.

decisions.choice: not in one day: one of several laws that protect a mother and her young
decisions.reason: Compare the law not to boil a young goat in its mother's milk (Exodus 23:19) and not to take a mother bird with her young (Deuteronomy 22:6-7). The text does not explain the reason, but these laws hold back from destroying parent and young together.

decisions.choice: a mother animal / a mother cow or sheep
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "mother", following m1.

records.gloss: And when you sacrifice [a] sacrifice of thanksgiving to Yahweh, for your acceptance you will sacrifice [it].
pieces: When you sacrifice a thanksgiving offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, do it in the way that will gain acceptance for you.

L.29: And when you sacrifice a sacrifice of thanksgiving to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for your acceptance you shall sacrifice [it].

R.29: When you give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a thanksgiving offering, do it the right way, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will accept you.

decisions.choice: a sacrifice of thanksgiving: a peace offering given to thank God
decisions.reason: It is one kind of peace offering, brought to thank God for help given (7:11-15; Psalm 107:22; 116:17). Its meat was eaten by the worshiper and the household.

decisions.choice: for your acceptance: offered by the rule, so that God accepts you
decisions.reason: See verse 19. Here the rule meant is the one in verse 30.

decisions.choice: do it in the way that will gain acceptance for you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "for your acceptance" into a clause; Readable makes the LORD the one who accepts.

records.source: בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ יֵאָכֵ֔ל לֹֽא־תוֹתִ֥ירוּ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ עַד־בֹּ֑קֶר אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: On the day that it will be eaten; not you will leave over of it until morning; I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: Eat it on the day it is offered, and keep none of it until the next morning. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.30: On that day it shall be eaten; you shall not leave any of it until morning. I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.30: Eat all of it on the day you offer it. Do not save any for the next morning. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: eaten on that day, none left until morning: the rule of 7:15
decisions.reason: The thanksgiving offering had to be eaten on the day it was offered (7:15). Other peace offerings could be eaten on the next day as well, but never on the third (7:16-18; 19:5-8).

records.gloss: And you will keep my commandments and do them; I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: You are to keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments and carry them out. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.31: And you shall keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments and do them. I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.31: Obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands and do what they say. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: keep and do: a closing call to obey
decisions.reason: The pair "keep and do" closes several sets of laws in this part of Leviticus (18:4-5; 19:37; 20:8, 22). It means both to guard the commandments and to carry them out.

records.source: וְלֹ֤א תְחַלְּלוּ֙ אֶת־שֵׁ֣ם קָדְשִׁ֔י וְנִ֨קְדַּשְׁתִּ֔י בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה מְקַדִּשְׁכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And not you will profane [the] name of my holiness, and I will be treated as holy in [the] midst of [the] sons of Israel; I [am] Yahweh [who] makes you holy,
pieces: Never profane {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name; among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} I must be treated as holy. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who makes you holy,

L.32: And you shall not profane {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name, and I will be treated as holy among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel. I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who makes you holy,

R.32: Do not dishonor {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} must honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as holy. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who makes you holy.

decisions.choice: I will be treated as holy: Israel must honor God as holy
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 10:3, where God shows himself holy among the priests. Here it is set against "you shall not profane my holy name": God is treated as holy when his people keep his name from being made common. Elsewhere God shows his holiness by what he does (Ezekiel 20:41; 36:23).

decisions.choice: I am the LORD who makes you holy: Israel's holiness is God's work
decisions.reason: The phrase closes the laws on holiness (20:8; 21:8, 15, 23; 22:9, 16), and here it is said to the whole people. Israel is to be holy (19:2), but it is God who makes them holy, by choosing them, bringing them out of Egypt (verse 33) and living among them. The holiness asked of them answers the holiness he gives (Exodus 31:13). Keeping his commands is how they live in it (20:8).

decisions.choice: dishonor; honor me as holy
decisions.reason: Readable says "dishonor" for "profane", as in verse 2, and puts the passive with Israel as the subject.

R.33: I brought you out of the land of Egypt so that I would be your God. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: who brought you out of Egypt to be your God: the ground of all these laws
decisions.reason: God's claim on Israel rests on the exodus (11:45; 19:36; 25:38; Exodus 20:2). He brought them out not only to free them but to be their God, and so they are to be his holy people.
